applied: practice.text: "A blocked diode holds up to the supply's peak" fails once a capacitor is added (i3): a half-wave diode feeding a capacitor holds about twice the peak. It is true of a bridge, the rectifier he will test, so scope it there.

analogy.text: A bridge throws itself at every zero crossing only with a resistor load; once a capacitor sits across the output (i3) the diodes conduct only near each peak, so the analogy needs its load stated.

explain.text: "Three-phase uses six diodes" is too general: a three-phase half-wave rectifier uses three and twelve-pulse rectifiers, common in large drives, use twelve; the six-diode circuit is the three-phase bridge.

interactive.whatAmILookingAt: Screen 9's "Three-phase uses six diodes" is too general, as in the explanation: three-phase half-wave and twelve-pulse rectifiers use other counts; the six-diode circuit is the three-phase bridge.
